newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia adds 8,456 new phone lines - paper.
newsitem.headline: Serbia adds 8,456 new phone lines - paper.

text.p: Serbia's postal and telecommunications company PTT Srbije has opened a new Siemens digital telephone exchange in Prokuplje with 8,456 phone lines, Belgrade daily Politika reported Tuesday.
The exchange, produced by the German company Siemens and assembled and installed by its Belgrade-based joint venture VF-TEL, has a capacity of 11,481 phone lines.
Total investment is in excess of 20 million dinars ($3.53 million).
The new exchange and an optical cable connecting Prokuplje, Kursumlija and Pristina will also enable connections to other networks such as E-mail, mobile telephony and Internet.

Serbia plans to install three million new lines by 2005 and double the number of lines to 40 per 100 inhabitants in a bid to upgrade its phone system which deteriorated during 3-1/2 years of sanctions and neglect.

"Serbia has already struck deals to increase the number of phone lines by 700,000 and the new exchange is an important step in the realisation of this programme," PTT Srbija deputy manager Slobodan Radulovic was quoted as saying.
